question.text: Will Argentina's Senate pass the 'Super RIGI' bill before January 1, 2027?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as **Yes** if, before January 1, 2027, the Argentine Senate approves the [Super RIGI](https://www.senado.gob.ar/parlamentario/comisiones/verExp/6.26/CD/PL) bill on the Senate floor, both in general and in particular.
question.fine_print: Approval of a version of the bill with amendments requiring the bill to return to the Chamber of Deputies still counts.

research:
Bottom line: as of 2026-10-27 the Super RIGI bill is still stuck in Senate committees. It has no committee report (dictamen) and no floor vote, and nothing found settles the question. The Senate has about six weeks of ordinary sessions left plus a possible December extension, and floor time is crowded by the budget and electoral reform.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-27 (checked today): The Senate file 6/26-CD-PL, "Super RIGI", shows Diputados passed it 2026-06-24 (Executive message 181/26). The Senate received it 2026-06-26 and sent it on 2026-07-13 to three committees: Presupuesto y Hacienda, Economía Nacional e Inversión, and Legislación General. No committee has reported it out, no dictamen text is posted and no floor vote is recorded. [Senado](https://www.senado.gob.ar/parlamentario/comisiones/verExp/6.26/CD/PL)

## 2. Current status
- Not settled. The bill has been frozen since early September. I found no report that the dictamen was signed after 2026-09-02, or that a floor session on it has been scheduled.
- Any Senate amendments, which are expected, would send the bill back to Diputados. Under the fine print that still counts as Yes.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-26: The Senate session set for Oct 22 was moved to Oct 29. Its agenda is the patent treaty (PCT), mental health reform, the carbon market and judicial nominations, with no Super RIGI. Tentative Senate sessions are Nov 19 and 26, and the ordinary period ends Nov 30. The electoral reform (ending the PASO primaries) is the Senate's priority, with a committee deadline of Nov 20. Activity may run into December. [Cronista](https://www.cronista.com/economia-politica/presupuesto-2027-el-gobierno-busca-cerrar-la-discusion-diputados-y-prepara-la-batalla-en-el-senado/)
- 2026-10-26/27: The government is rushing the 2027 Budget and the "Malvinas"/Sovereignty law ahead of Pope León XIV's visit, expected Nov 8-11, which will slow Congress in early November. [El Destape](https://www.eldestapeweb.com/politica/congreso-marcha-lla-busca-dictaminar-presupuesto-2027-ley-soberania-nacional-antes-llegada-papa-20261026183917)
- 2026-10-18: The government is making a "last attempt" to unblock the bill. The Economy Ministry (Caputo) drafted a counterproposal for senators Abad (UCR), Espínola (non-Kirchnerist Peronism) and Goerling (PRO). It would not meet all their demands, the main one being a 15% price preference for local suppliers. A decision was expected "in the coming days." [Río Negro](https://www.rionegro.com.ar/politica/el-panorama-del-super-rigi-en-el-congreso-aliados-piden-cambios-y-el-proyecto-volveria-a-diputados-4763141/); [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/politica/2026/10/18/el-gobierno-quiere-destrabar-el-super-rigi-en-el-senado-y-le-hizo-una-contrapropuesta-a-los-aliados/)
- 2026-09-03: Infobae reported growing doubts about the political reform after this setback, and that the government thinks its allies are "raising their price." [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/politica/2026/09/03/tras-el-reves-con-el-super-rigi-en-el-senado-crecen-las-dudas-sobre-la-reforma-politica-y-para-el-gobierno-los-aliados-se-suben-el-precio/)
- 2026-09-02: The joint committee meeting failed to produce a dictamen: the ruling LLA collected about 20 of the 26 signatures needed, and committee chair Monteverde (LLA) suspended the meeting. Senate LLA leader Bullrich said: "If it has so many problems, we'll stay with the RIGI." The planned floor dates of Sept 10 and 17 fell through. [iProfesional](https://www.iprofesional.com/politica/463625-super-rigi-vuelve-a-trabarse-en-el-senado-y-abre-conflicto-para-milei-y-bullrich); [Parlamentario](https://www.parlamentario.com/2026/09/02/los-aliados-pidieron-mas-cambios-y-el-oficialismo-no-pudo-dictaminar-el-super-rigi/)
- 2026-09-01: The government accepted two changes: a stronger "buy national" requirement and own power generation or substations for data centers. [Tiempo Argentino](https://www.tiempoar.com.ar/ta_article/se-dictamina-con-modificaciones-el-super-rigi-en-el-senado-y-volveria-a-diputados/)
- 2026-08-19: Committee hearings were held, with no dictamen in sight. [Parlamentario](https://www.parlamentario.com/2026/08/19/aun-sin-despacho-a-la-vista-el-senado-escucho-a-expositores-que-cuestionaron-el-super-rigi/)
- 2026-06-24: Diputados approved it 130-106 with 7 abstentions. [HCDN](https://www.hcdn.gob.ar/prensa/noticia/DIPUTADOS-LE-DIO-MEDIA-SANCION-AL-SUPER-RIGI-QUE-INCENTIVA-GRANDES-INVERSIONES-EN-NUEVAS-INDUSTRIAS/)

## 4. Base rates
- I found no systematic base rate. Comparable precedent: the original RIGI was part of the Ley Bases, which the Senate passed in June 2024 with amendments, about 1.5 months after Diputados and after long negotiation with the same kind of allied blocs. [Diario de Cuyo](https://www.diariodecuyo.com.ar/argentina/el-senado-aprobo-la-ley-bases-y-milei-gana-su-primera-batalla-1627368.html)
- The Senate still amends government economic bills in 2026: it changed the Central Bank reform (66-2 on Aug 26). Several bills passed by Diputados have sat for years, for example the gambling-addiction bill from Nov 2024.
- The Super RIGI has now been in committee for about 4 months, and its dictamen has been stalled for about 8 weeks.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the supplied Kalshi or Polymarket markets match this question; they cover US Senate races, Italy and similar. I found no market or expert forecast on the Super RIGI.
- The closest related signal: Polymarket gives Milei a 46.5% chance of winning Argentina's 2027 presidential election.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-10-28/29: Senate session (Super RIGI not on its agenda). The government's decision on the Caputo counterproposal is still pending.
- 2026-10-29: Caputo, Karina Milei and Santilli attend the RIGI investment business rounds in Rosario, where officials might say something about the Super RIGI. [Cadena 3](https://www.cadena3.com/noticia/noticias-rosario/caputo-karina-milei-y-santilli-estaran-este-jueves-en-rosario-para-la-ronda-de-negocios-del-rigi_606955)
- 2026-11-03: US elections, with lawmakers traveling. 2026-11-08 to 11: papal visit.
- 2026-11-18: Diputados plans to vote on the 2027 Budget, which then goes to the Senate.
- 2026-11-19 and 26: tentative Senate sessions. 2026-11-20: committee deadline for the electoral reform. 2026-11-30: ordinary sessions end.
- December: any extraordinary sessions must be called by the Executive, and the Super RIGI would have to be on that agenda. On the composition of the Senate from Dec 10, I found nothing specific.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left and what Yes requires.** About 9 weeks remain, until 2027-01-01. For Yes, the Senate committees (Presupuesto, Economía Nacional, Legislación General) must issue a dictamen with at least 26 signatures. The bill must then go to the floor, where it needs approval both in general and in particular. This can happen in the remaining ordinary sessions (tentatively Nov 19 and 26, ending Nov 30) or in December extraordinary sessions, if the Executive puts it on the agenda. Amendments that send it back to Diputados still count.

(b) **Status quo.** The bill is frozen in committee with no dictamen since the failed Sept 2 meeting. If nothing changes, the answer is No.

(c) **Base rate.** Executive economic bills that pass Diputados and then stall in Senate committee for 2 or more months, with only about 2 months left in the year, pass by year end perhaps 20-30% of the time. The Ley Bases is the counterexample: it passed after tough negotiation, but it was a top priority and had not stalled. Many other bills sit indefinitely. I start at about 25%.

(d) **Evidence.**
- **For Yes:**
  - On 2026-10-18 the Economy Ministry drafted a counterproposal for the key allied senators (Abad, Espínola, Goerling), a "last attempt" with a decision expected soon.
  - On 2026-09-01 the government had already accepted some changes, and on Sept 2 it was only about 6 signatures short.
  - Milei's government has used December extraordinary sessions before.
  - The Senate's composition does not change on Dec 10, 2026.
- **For No:**
  - Senate LLA leader Bullrich said on 2026-09-02 "we'll stay with the RIGI," which signals a willingness to drop the bill.
  - The bill has been stalled for 8 weeks, and the counterproposal does not meet the allies' main demand (the 15% price preference).
  - The 2026-10-29 session agenda excludes it.
  - Floor time is crowded by the 2027 Budget (arriving after Nov 18) and electoral reform (the priority), and the papal visit takes time out in early November.

(e) **Scenarios.**
- **No:** The allies reject Caputo's counterproposal. The government prioritizes the Budget and the end of the PASO primaries, and the Super RIGI is left out of December extraordinary sessions or not reached. It carries into 2027.
- **Yes:** The allies accept a compromise in early November and the dictamen is signed. The Senate passes it with amendments on Nov 26 or in a December extraordinary session, packaged with the Budget, and it returns to Diputados.

(f) **Adjustment.** I start at about 25%. An active counterproposal and an ally gap of only a few signatures pull me slightly up. The leadership's signaled willingness to drop it, the crowded calendar and the fact that the bill is not on upcoming agendas pull me down. There is no matching market to anchor on. The net is slightly below the base rate.

Probability: 21%

(a) About 9 weeks remain (to Jan 1, 2027). For Yes, the Senate must first issue a committee dictamen (roughly 26 signatures across three committees). It must then hold a floor session approving the Super RIGI in general and in particular, either in the ordinary period ending Nov 30 or in December extraordinary sessions, which require the Executive to put the bill on the agenda. Amendments that send the bill back to Diputados still count.

(b) Status quo: the bill has been stuck in committee since the failed dictamen on Sept 2, with no session scheduled. If nothing changes, the answer is No.

(c) Base rate: there is no clean reference class. Bills passed by Diputados that stall in Senate committee for 2 months or more, with no dictamen and under 10 weeks left, rarely pass in that window. I would put that at roughly 15-25%. Government-priority economic bills under Milei have done better, since the Ley Bases eventually passed with amendments, so I would raise the anchor to about 25%.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- Oct 18: the Economy Ministry drafted a counterproposal to the holdout senators (Abad, Espínola, Goerling), so the government is still pushing.
- The government accepted concessions on Sept 1.
- LLA already had about 20 of the 26 signatures.
- Tentative sessions on Nov 19 and 26, plus December extraordinaries, give windows. The bill could also be traded alongside the budget.

Evidence for No:
- The dictamen has been stalled for 8 weeks.
- Bullrich said on Sept 2: "If it has so many problems, we'll stay with the RIGI."
- The Oct 29 session agenda excludes the bill.
- Floor time is crowded by the budget (arriving after Nov 18), the electoral reform priority and the papal visit (Nov 8-11).
- The allies' core demand (a 15% local-supplier preference) is not met by the counterproposal.

(e) No scenario: the allies reject the counterproposal and the Senate spends November on the electoral reform and the budget. The Executive then leaves the Super RIGI out of the December extraordinaries, or it is listed but never reaches the floor.

Yes scenario: in early November a deal adds a partial local-preference clause, and the dictamen is signed mid-November. The Senate then approves the bill with amendments on Nov 26 or in a December extraordinary session alongside the budget, and it returns to Diputados.

(f) I start at about 25%. The status quo has been static for 8 weeks and the agenda is crowded, which pushes down. Ongoing government negotiation and the near-complete signature count push up modestly. Net, I land slightly below the anchor, at around 20%.

Probability: 20%

(a) About 9 weeks remain, until Jan 1, 2027. For Yes, the Senate committees must issue a dictamen (26 signatures), and the Senate floor must then approve the bill in general and in particular. Approval with amendments, which would send it back to Diputados, still counts. The vote has to happen in the November sessions (Nov 19 or 26, before ordinary sessions end Nov 30) or in December extraordinary sessions, which only happen if the Executive includes the bill in its call.

(b) Status quo: the bill has sat in three committees for about 4 months, and the dictamen has been stalled for about 8 weeks. If nothing changes, the answer is No.

(c) Base rate: when a Diputados-passed government economic bill is stalled in Senate committee with no dictamen and about 2 months left in the legislative year, maybe 20-30% pass the Senate within that window. The Ley Bases is a counterexample: it passed after about 1.5 months of hard negotiation, but it was a top priority. Many other bills sit for years. Starting point: about 25%.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - On Oct 18 the government made a "last attempt" with a Caputo counterproposal to Abad, Espínola and Goerling, so it still wants the bill.
  - The September dictamen fell only about 6 signatures short.
  - The allies' demands (local-supplier preference) are narrow and negotiable.
  - December extraordinary sessions are routinely called under Milei.
- **For No:**
  - On Sept 2, Bullrich said "we'll stay with the RIGI," signaling lower priority.
  - Super RIGI is not on the Oct 29 agenda.
  - Floor time is crowded by the 2027 Budget (Diputados votes Nov 18, then the Senate), the electoral reform (committee deadline Nov 20), the Sovereignty law and the papal visit (Nov 8-11).
  - The counterproposal does not meet the allies' main demand.
  - As of Oct 27 there is no news of a deal.

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** the allies reject the counterproposal or talks drag on. November floor time goes to the electoral reform and the budget, and the December extraordinary agenda focuses on the budget, so the Super RIGI slips to 2027.
- **Yes:** a deal on the local-preference clause comes in early November. The dictamen is signed mid-November, and the Senate approves the bill with amendments on Nov 26, or in a December extraordinary session packaged alongside the budget.

(f) I start at 25%. The live counterproposal and the near-miss on signatures push up slightly. The total lack of scheduling, the crowded calendar, Bullrich's de-prioritization, and the need for both a dictamen and a floor vote within about 5 effective weeks push down. Net, I land slightly below the base rate, around 22%.

Probability: 22%

(a) About 9 weeks remain, until January 1, 2027. For Yes, the Super RIGI bill (6/26-CD-PL) needs a committee dictamen, which requires about 6 more signatures than the roughly 20 LLA had. It then needs a floor session where it passes both in general and in particular. That session could fall in the ordinary period (tentative dates Nov 19 and 26, ending Nov 30) or in December extraordinary sessions, if the Executive puts the bill on that agenda. Amendments sending it back to Diputados still count.

(b) Status quo: the bill stays in committee and the question resolves No. It has had no movement since the failed dictamen on Sept 2, and it is not on the Oct 29 agenda.

(c) Base rate: government-priority bills that Diputados passed but that then stalled in the Senate for about 2 months without a dictamen, with under 10 weeks left in the year, rarely pass by year-end. My rough estimate is 15-25%. The Ley Bases is a counterexample: it passed after long negotiation, but without a comparably long stall.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- Oct 18: the government is making a "last attempt," with a Caputo counterproposal to the pivotal senators Abad, Espínola and Goerling. A decision was expected within days.
- Sept 1: the government already accepted some changes, so allies are bargaining rather than rejecting the bill outright.
- The Milei government has used December extraordinary sessions before.
- The investment push, including the Oct 29 RIGI business rounds, shows continued executive interest.

Evidence for No:
- Sept 2: the dictamen failed, and Bullrich said "we'll stay with the RIGI."
- Oct 26: the Senate agenda excludes the bill, and floor time is crowded by the budget (arriving after Nov 18), the electoral reform and the papal visit.
- The counterproposal does not meet allies' main demand, the 15% local preference.
- Allies are "raising their price" across several bills.

(e) No scenario: the counterproposal is rejected or ignored, the budget and PASO reform absorb November and December, and the Super RIGI slips to 2027.

Yes scenario: a deal on local-content preference is struck in early November, the dictamen is signed mid-November, and the bill is voted with amendments on Nov 26 or in a December extraordinary session alongside the budget.

(f) I start from about 20%. The active government counterproposal keeps a live path open, so I don't go lower. The crowded calendar, the 8-week stall and the gap on the allies' main demand keep me from going higher. No market covers this question. I land at about 18%.

Probability: 18%

**(a) Time left and what Yes requires.** There are about 9 weeks until January 1, 2027. For Yes, the Senate must approve the Super RIGI bill (file 6/26-CD-PL) on the floor, both in general and in particular. First it needs a committee report (dictamen) signed by 26 members across the three committees, and then a floor session. Approval with amendments that send it back to Diputados still counts.

**(b) Status quo.** The bill has sat in committee since July 13, and the dictamen has been stalled since September 2. It is not on the October 29 agenda. If nothing changes, the answer is No.

**(c) Base rate.** Some bills passed by Diputados are stuck in Senate committee with a failed dictamen attempt and roughly 2 months left in the year. Among those, perhaps 15-25% pass the Senate within that window. Bills that still have active executive backing and an ongoing negotiation do better than abandoned ones. The original RIGI, inside the Ley Bases, passed with amendments after a long negotiation with the same kind of allied blocs, which is a supportive precedent. Base rate: about 20%.

**(d) Strongest evidence.**
- For Yes:
  - On October 18 the Economy Ministry drafted a counterproposal for the key holdout senators (Abad, Espínola and Goerling), so the government is still actively pushing.
  - On September 2, LLA already had about 20 of the 26 signatures needed.
  - On September 1 the government had already accepted some changes.
  - December extraordinary sessions, which Milei has called in past years, could include the bill.
- For No:
  - The September 2 dictamen failure, and Bullrich's comment that "we'll stay with the RIGI."
  - Eight weeks of stall, and allies "raising their price."
  - The counterproposal does not meet the main demand, the 15% price preference for local suppliers.
  - Floor time is crowded by the 2027 Budget, which reaches the Senate after November 18, and by the electoral reform, which is the priority.
  - The papal visit on November 8-11 and the US elections will slow Congress.

**(e) Scenarios.**
- No: The allies reject the counterproposal or keep stalling. The Senate spends late November and December on the Budget and electoral reform, and the Super RIGI is either left off the extraordinary agenda or never gets a dictamen.
- Yes: In early November the government concedes a partial local-preference clause. The dictamen is signed mid-November, and the bill passes with amendments on November 26 or in a December extraordinary session alongside the Budget.

**(f) Adjustment.** I start from 20%. Active government engagement and a near-complete signature count push up slightly. The crowded calendar, the unmet core demand and Bullrich's signal of willingness to drop the bill push down. The net is roughly unchanged, at about 20%.

Probability: 20%
